newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK budget fails to improve HK competiveness - Peat.
newsitem.headline: HK budget fails to improve HK competiveness - Peat.

text.p: Hong Kong's cautious 1997/98 transitional budget contained no substantive fiscal measures to improve the territory's role as a regional financial and service centre, accountancy firm Peat Marwick said on Wednesday.
Financial Secretary Donald Tsang announced a windfall budget surplus for 1996/97 of HK$15.1 billion but resisted calls to cut the corporate tax rate which currently stands at 16.5 percent.
He announced a review of the tax system to see if Hong Kong's business environment can be improved.

"I would like to see the government take a more proactive role in maintaining Hong Kong's position of pre-eminence and competitiveness as a regional and international business, financial and services centre," said KPMG Peat Marwick tax partner Jennifer Wong.

"The proposed amendment to the Inland Revenue Ordinance in relation to the deductibility of foreign withholding tax, while reflecting current Inland Revenue Department practice, does not represent any significant inducement to encourage overseas companies to set up branch operations in Hong Kong, thereby strengthening (Hong Kong's) status as an international financial centre.
"Fiscal measures alone will not address the structural problems related to the increasing cost of doing business in the territory."
The high cost of property represents the single greatest threat to Hong Kong's competitiveness and the Financial Secretary did not offer any measures to counter the problem, she added.
